extracted.intended_audience: cognitive neuroscientists, psychologists and fMRI researchers studying humor/affective processing
extracted.subtask_description: Designing and reporting an event-related fMRI experiment to dissociate cognitive (semantic/phonological juxtaposition) and affective (amusement) components of humor using semantic jokes and puns, behavioral judgments, and appropriate imaging contrasts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Isolate cognitive and affective components
rubrics_metrics.description: Design contrasts that separate the cognitive juxtaposition of mental sets (required to 'get' a joke) from the affective feeling of amusement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use contrasts of (jokes – matched baselines) to identify cognitive processing associated with juxtaposition; use comparisons of subjectively funny vs subjectively non-funny jokes (within-subject, joke-by-joke) to isolate affective components while controlling for the cognitive processing that occurs in both. Perform conjunction analyses across joke types (semantic and phonological) masked by the main effect of jokes to identify common affective regions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use stimulus categories that probe different cognitive processes
rubrics_metrics.description: Include both semantic jokes and phonological jokes (puns) to test modality/type-specific cognitive networks.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present equal sets (here: 30 semantic, 30 phonological) and compare each joke type to its own non-joke baseline to reveal type-specific networks (e.g., semantic juxtapositions recruit bilateral temporal regions; phonological juxtapositions recruit left inferior frontal/insula). Directly compare semantic vs phonological joke activations (masked by main effect) to demonstrate anatomical dissociation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Construct matched baseline conditions
rubrics_metrics.description: Use baseline stimuli that preserve setup lines but replace punch lines with merely descriptive (non-joke) answers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: keep the setup identical but alter the punch to a descriptive answer (e.g., replace 'Their personalities' with 'The pill'). Baselines control for processing of setup material so the contrast highlights juxtaposition/punch-specific processes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Balance acoustic/temporal properties of stimuli
rubrics_metrics.description: Balance items across experimental conditions for number of phonemes and temporal duration and present stimuli prerecorded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ensure stimuli are edited to precise temporal lengths and matched across conditions to prevent low-level auditory or timing confounds. In this study stimuli were prerecorded voice files, balanced for phoneme count and duration.

rubrics_metrics.name: Randomize presentation order
rubrics_metrics.description: Present stimuli in a random order during scanning to avoid order effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Random ordering of semantic and phonological items (and their baselines) reduces predictability and confounds from sequence effects.

rubrics_metrics.name: Collect in-scan behavioral judgments and post-scan ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: While scanned, have subjects make immediate binary judgments (amusing/not) by keypress; collect finer-grained post-scan funniness ratings (1–5).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Immediate judgments provide trial-by-trial affective responses for in-scan contrasts (funny vs not funny); post-scan ratings enable parametric covariation (e.g., correlating MVPFC activation with subjective funniness). Instruct subjects to refrain from laughter to minimize head movement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Subject/sample characteristics and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: Report key sample details such as handedness, health status, and sample size.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example study scanned 14 right-handed normal subjects; include ethics approval and correspondence details. Handedness matters for lateralization interpretations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Event-related fMRI timing and acquisition parameters
rubrics_metrics.description: Use a time-locked single-event design with specified setup/pause/punch timing and appropriate TR, jitter, slice thickness, and sequence sensitive to BOLD.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example parameters: setup line durations 1340–3230 ms (mean 2420 ms), mean pause 1580 ms, punch delivered at 4000 ms lasting 480–3250 ms (mean 1540 ms). Acquire whole-brain T2*-weighted echoplanar images (48 slices, 1.8 mm thick with 1.2 mm gap, 64×64 matrix, 3×3 mm pixels; TE 40 ms) on a 2T system, TR = 4.1 s, random jitter of 1 TR. Sample BOLD signal as an HRF at the midpoint between punch-line presentation and motor response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Statistical analysis framework and contrasts
rubrics_metrics.description: Use an established SPM random-effects analysis with clearly specified contrasts (main effects, simple effects, direct comparisons, conjunctions) and appropriate masking.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: analyzed with SPM99 using a random effects model. Main effect: (semantic jokes + phonological jokes) – (semantic baseline + phonological baseline). Simple main effects: each joke type vs its baseline. Direct comparisons and masked contrasts reveal dissociations (e.g., semantic – phonological and reverse). Conjunction: (funny semantic – not funny semantic) ∧ (funny phonological – not funny phonological) masked by main effect to isolate common affective regions. Control for cognitive processing when contrasting funny vs not-funny. Report statistical thresholds and multiple-comparison correction (e.g., report activations significant at p < 0.05 corrected where applicable).

rubrics_metrics.name: Parametric/covariation analyses with subjective ratings
rubrics_metrics.description: Test whether regional activations covary with continuous subjective measures (e.g., post-scan funniness ratings).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: MVPFC activation covaried with post-scan funniness ratings (p < 0.05, corrected). Use covariation to link neural activation to subjective affective magnitude.

rubrics_metrics.name: Control cognitive confounds when isolating affect
rubrics_metrics.description: When contrasting funny vs non-funny trials, ensure both conditions involve similar cognitive processing so differences reflect affective processes.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Perform subject-by-subject, item-wise comparisons so that cognitive processing related to resolving the punch line is present in both conditions; this helps ensure group differences reflect pleasure/amusement rather than comprehension differences.

rubrics_metrics.name: Interpret anatomical activations in light of functional neuroanatomy and lesion literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Relate observed activations to known functional roles (e.g., semantic processing, speech production, reward) and compare with lesion study findings.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example interpretations: posterior temporal lobe involvement indicates semantic integration; left inferior frontal and insula implicate phonological/speech-related processing; MVPFC relates to reward and affective valuation. Use prior lesion and imaging studies to contextualize whether activations reflect integrative semantic processes or affective components.
